suggestions.title: Incorporate Emergency Patching SLAs
suggestions.detail: The SOP mentions applying patches in Section 6.3 but lacks the specific timeframe defined in Risk Control CC-007 (Monthly cycle vs 72 hours for CVSS â¥ 9.0).
suggestions.proposed_text: Applying security patches to address the vulnerability exploited. For vulnerabilities with a CVSS score â¥ 9.0, emergency patching must be completed within 72 hours as per CC-007.
suggestions.original_text: Applying security patches to address the vulnerability exploited

suggestions.title: Add Mandatory Regulatory Reporting Timelines
suggestions.detail: The SOP lacks specific reporting windows required by Indian regulators (RBI/CERT-In) as implied by CC-014.
suggestions.proposed_text: The Legal/Compliance team will coordinate mandatory reporting. Note: Cybersecurity incidents must be reported to CERT-In within 6 hours of detection as per the 2022 Directions. Significant incidents must be reported to RBI within the timeframes specified in the Cyber Security Framework.
suggestions.original_text: The Legal team will advise if law enforcement involvement is required

suggestions.title: Reference Incident-Specific Playbooks
suggestions.detail: Section 6.2 provides generic containment steps. Risk Control CC-013 explicitly mentions defined incident response playbooks which should be utilised here.
suggestions.proposed_text: Containment actions should be executed according to the specific Incident Response Playbook (e.g., Ransomware, Phishing, DDoS) as defined in CC-013. General actions include:

suggestions.title: Formalise Post-Incident Review (PIR)
suggestions.detail: The SOP ends at documentation but lacks a 'Lessons Learned' phase, which is critical for the 'continual improvement' noted in the document notes.
suggestions.proposed_text: Documentation should be completed as soon as practicable. Within 5 business days of incident closure, the Incident Response Manager shall convene a Post-Incident Review (PIR) to identify lessons learned and update the SOP or playbooks accordingly.
suggestions.original_text: Documentation should be completed as soon as practicable after the incident is resolved.

suggestions.title: Define IR Drill Frequency
suggestions.detail: Section 9 uses the vague term 'periodically' for exercises, while Risk Control CC-013 specifies a semi-annual frequency.
suggestions.proposed_text: Tabletop exercises and BCP/DR simulations shall be conducted semi-annually to test and validate the bank's incident response readiness, in alignment with CC-013.
suggestions.original_text: Tabletop exercises and simulations may be conducted periodically to test the bank's incident response readiness.

suggestions.title: Resolve owner conflict for CC-013
suggestions.detail: The SOP step assigns ownership to IT Operations, while the RCM lists IT / BCP Team for control CC-013. This is suggested because SOP and RCM ownership must align before the control can be tested consistently.
suggestions.proposed_text: Clarify the accountable owner for control CC-013. If the RCM is correct, state that IT / BCP Team owns the control and describe the hand-off from IT Operations; otherwise update the RCM owner and keep the SOP wording aligned.
suggestions.original_text: Restore systems from backups and verify integrity

The following roles are involved in the incident response process. Each team should be aware of their responsibilities and be ready to act when an incident occurs.

Note: A formal RACI matrix has not been defined. Ownership may be unclear during multi-team incidents.

| Role | Responsibilities |
| --- | --- |
| CISO | Overall accountability for cybersecurity. Should be informed of significant incidents. |

| Incident Response Manager | Manages the response process and communication during an incident. Usually the IT Security Head. |
| IT Operations | Supports containment and recovery activities as directed by the security team. |
| Legal / Compliance | Advises on regulatory and legal obligations. Involved when required. |
| Senior Management | Should be kept informed of major incidents that affect the business. |
| HR Department | Involved in cases where an employee is suspected of wrongdoing. |

edit_targets.target_text:
The following roles are involved in the incident response process. Each team should be aware of their responsibilities and be ready to act when an incident occurs.

Note: A formal RACI matrix has not been defined. Ownership may be unclear during multi-team incidents.

| Role | Responsibilities |
| --- | --- |
| CISO | Overall accountability for cybersecurity. Should be informed of significant incidents. |
| IT Security Team / SOC | Monitors security alerts, conducts triage, coordinates response activities. |
| Incident Response Manager | Manages the response process and communication during an incident. Usually the IT Security Head. |
| IT Operations | Supports containment and recovery activities as directed by the security team. |
| Legal / Compliance | Advises on regulatory and legal obligations. Involved when required. |
| Senior Management | Should be kept informed of major incidents that affect the business. |
| HR Department | Involved in cases where an employee is suspected of wrongdoing. |

suggestions.title: Add SOP coverage for CC-016
suggestions.detail: The RCM contains control CC-016, but no matching process step was found in the primary SOP. This is suggested because the SOP should describe the control procedure that auditors will test against the RCM.
suggestions.proposed_text: Add a procedure step for control CC-016 owned by Physical Security. The step should describe Biometric access control and CCTV surveillance at all data centre entry points; visitor escort policy enforced and identify retained evidence: the relevant control evidence.

edit_targets.target_text:
Not all security events are incidents. When an alert is received, the SOC analyst should assess whether it represents a genuine incident or a false positive.

Incidents should be classified based on their potential impact to the organisation. Higher impact incidents should be escalated to senior management and the CISO as appropriate.

Note: No formal severity classification schema (e.g., P1âP4) with defined criteria, escalation timeframes, or SLAs is included in this version of the SOP.

Factors to consider when assessing impact include:

Number of systems or users affected

Sensitivity of data involved

Whether services have been disrupted

Likelihood of financial loss or reputational damage
